Title: Diagnosis of test `testOverrideMeanWithMathClass` failure

Details: 
The test `testOverrideMeanWithMathClass` intends to verify that overriding the default mean implementation in `SummaryStatistics` with a new instance of `Mean` works correctly. The test creates an array `scores` of doubles, creates a `SummaryStatistics` instance `stats`, overrides its mean implementation via `setMeanImpl(new Mean())`, adds all score values to `stats`, and finally asserts that `stats.getMean()` equals the result of a fresh `Mean()` instance's `evaluate(scores)`.

From the investigation of relevant methods:

- `SummaryStatistics.setMeanImpl(StorelessUnivariateStatistic)` is called at the start after the object is created. It invokes `checkEmpty()`, which throws an exception if there are any values added (`n > 0`). This confirms that the mean implementation can only be overridden if no data has been previously added, which matches the test's setup since overriding is done before adding any values.

- Adding values is done by `SummaryStatistics.addValue(double)`. Its code shows it increments sums, moments, min, max, sum of logs, and also increments `meanImpl` unless it is a `Mean` instance. Specifically:
  ```java
  if (!(meanImpl instanceof Mean)) {
      meanImpl.increment(value);
  }
  ```
  This means if the `meanImpl` is an instance of `Mean` (like in the test), it is NOT incremented when values are added. Therefore, the internal mean computation in `stats` will not accumulate data when the mean implementation is set to a `Mean` instance.

- Consequently, when the final assertion compares `stats.getMean()` with `new Mean().evaluate(scores)`, the `stats.getMean()` retrieves the mean result from `meanImpl.getResult()`. Since no values were fed to `meanImpl` (increment was skipped), it will likely return a default or incorrect result (probably zero), causing the test to fail.

- The `Mean.evaluate(double[])` method calculates mean over the array properly, so the right expected value is computed.

Summary: The bug is caused because `SummaryStatistics.addValue` explicitly skips incrementing the `meanImpl` if it is an instance of `Mean`. When the test overrides the mean implementation with a new `Mean` instance, the mean statistic does not get incremented with new values, resulting in `stats.getMean()` returning an incorrect value.

This is possibly a design flaw or assumption in the class that the default `meanImpl` is always a `Mean` subclass, and hence it optimizes out increments only if it is the default one. But the test shows that overriding it with a new `Mean` instance breaks this assumption.

---

Suggested methods to fix:
org.apache.commons.math.stat.descriptive.SummaryStatistics.addValue(double)
org.apache.commons.math.stat.descriptive.SummaryStatistics.setMeanImpl(org.apache.commons.math.stat.descriptive.StorelessUnivariateStatistic)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
